text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Deputy Economics Minister Jozef Brhel said Slovakia was considering unspecified relief in custom duties for imports of high-tech equipment, effective from the beginning of next year.
- Brhel said he expected foreign banks to be dominant in providing loans for Slovak companies in 1996. Last year foreign banks accounted for about half of the loans extended.
- Slovakia's major producer of steel pipe, Zeleziarne Podbrezova, said the European Union's anti-dumping procedures against it were unfounded.

- Production of Zeleziarne Podbrezova totalled 1.6 billion crowns in the first half of this year, with the pre-tax profit totalling 50.8 million crowns. The company's exports totalled 1.24 billion crowns, mostly to European Union and the Czech Republic.
- Steel producer VSZ said it held talks with unspecified Canadian companies on possible use of VSZ's production in Canadian construction sector.

- Tyre producer Matador Puchov has launched production in its joint-venture in Russian town Omsk. The new company should produce 250,000 tyres this year, with output increasing to one million next year and to three million tyres a year within the next three years.
- The Slovak Antimonopoly Bureau reviewed 39 cases of alleged cartel agreements violating the competition law last year, compared with 21 cases in 1994 and 12 cases in 1993.

PRAVDA - Germany's largest bank, Deutsche Bank, said it would help create a fund to support Slovak medium-sezed companies, according to Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar who was speaking after talks with bank officials.

- Meciar said the discussion with Deutsche Bank officials included possibilities of the bank's loan activities in Slovakia and its direct entry to the restructuring process of the economy, mainly the engineering industry.
- Meciar said Deutsche Bank will present itself to the Slovak banking community by the end of this year.
- The finance ministry denied information that Deputy Finance Minister Jozef Magula was leaving his post.
SME - Ivan Lexa, head of the secret police (SIS), will discuss possible further cooperation with the director of the Russian foreign intelligence service on Thursday.
NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia's gross domestic product per capita, at present, totals only about 30 percent of the Austrian figure.
